scope: Customer name changes and receiver mentions during cart building, payment selection and final review
baselineFindings: CRITICAL: in awaiting_final_confirm «el pedido va a nombre de Laura Gómez» CREATED THE ORDER without «confirmar»: the compound parser removed the explicit name and the leftover «el pedido va» matched isConfirmKeyword («va» is an approval word)
«cambia el nombre a Carlos» answered «No tenemos esos productos en la carta» and dropped the final step to building_cart
«el nombre es Laura», «no, el nombre es Carlos», «que lo reciba Laura» were dropped silently (cart or payment prompt re-shown)
«mi nombre es Carlos Pérez» in the final step changed the name silently and asked «¿Algo más?»
«ponlo a nombre de mi esposa Laura» stored «mi esposa Laura» as the name
«soy alérgico al maní» stored «alérgico al maní» as the customer name
fix: tryHandleCustomerNameChange (before the contact/name label block and the compound parser): explicit forms (el/mi nombre es, cambia el nombre a, va/queda a nombre de, ponlo a nombre de, a nombre de, mi nombre es, me llamo) with optional «no,/mejor/perdón» lead update the name with an acknowledgement; relation prefixes (mi esposa, mi mamá…) are dropped; «que lo reciba X» is an order note. State is preserved; the final step re-shows the summary and asks for «confirmar». Names that look like addresses, catalog products or checkout words keep their routes. Defensive guard in the compound parser: after an explicit name was extracted in awaiting_final_confirm, an empty or approval-only remainder re-shows the summary instead of approving. tryHandleExplicitCustomerNameLabel rejects «soy <condition>» (alérgico, vegetariano, celíaco, … or phrases with al/con/sin).
knownGaps: «soy X» still updates the name through the existing route without the new acknowledgement wording
Name plus other instructions in one message (name + address change) keep existing routes
